newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Dragon Oil sees growth in Caspian.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Dragon Oil sees growth in Caspian.

text.p: Irish-based oil and exploration company Dragon Oil Plc said on Friday it expects its Caspian Sea oil production to increase to 75,000 barrels per day (bpd) in the next five years, from 6,200 bpd now.
"The Caspian will probably remain the core area (for Dragon) in the short-term," finance director Graeme Thomson told Reuters
Dragon Oil purchased its Caspian Sea interest in May, 1996.
Earlier the group announced a three-for-five rights issue to raise around 65 million pounds ($106 million) before expenses to fund development of its Caspian Sea well, offshore Turkmenistan.
The funds will also help fund an appraisal of its natural gas discovery offshore in Thailand, as well as its intention to seek new licence and producing interests.
Dragon Oil plans to offer up to 3.24 billion new shares at 2.0 (British) pence, raising some 62.5 million stg net of expenses.

The two largest shareholders in Dragon Oil, chairman Arifin Panigoro's Satellite Overseas Ltd (SOL) and Sinophil Corp, have irrevocably undertaken to take up their entitlements of 1,500 million and 603.2 million shares, representing 46.3 percent and 18.6 percent respectively of the company's shares.
The fact both have taken up their entitlements "indicates a very strong belief in the asset base of the group and the way things are going," said Thomson.
Panigoro's latest undertaking represents an injection of 30 million stg, having put in 38 million stg last year.
Davy Corporate Finance Ltd has underwritten the balance of the rights issue.

Dragon Oil purchased a 60 percent stake in Larmag Energy Assets Ltd (LEA), a 50-50 offshore joint venture with Turkmenistan, in May last year. The rights issue will cover all the costs of developing the Block II well in the Caspian through to early 1999.

Since taking up its 30 percent stake in Block II, output has increased from some 4,600 bpd to 6,200 bpd currently. It has also seen proven and probable hydrocarbon reserves grow from 48 to 165 million barrels of oil equivalent.
"Obviously (1996) was a year of big change," said Thomson of the purchase of the Caspian Sea stake. "We are moving very quickly away from what was our traditional base in North America".

In January, the group took up a 30.5 percent stake in an offshore gas discovery on Block B12/32 in the Gulf of Thailand, operated by Texaco Inc, which has a flow rate of 21 million cubic feet per day.
The group is also participating in four offshore licences or applications in the Philippines, covering a total area of more the 45,000 square km.
Dragon Oil reported a pretax loss of $414,000 in the year to December 31, 1997, down from a loss of $1.51 million a year ago.

Thomson said the new year was looking to go "very well" but it was too early to say whether the group would achieve a profit on a pretax basis. But, he noted it made a net profit in 1996 of $539,000 after a net loss of $1.35 million the year before.

"We remain convinced of the potential in our current asset base," chairman Panigoro said in the results statement. "With the proceeds of the rights issue and with the operational foundations laid in the last year, Dragon's growth prospects are clearly enhanced".
